---
title: "General solutions: one-variable models"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, chapter 6, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

Equilibria and their stability describe where a model goes. A general
solution says how it gets there: `n(t)` as a function of time and the initial
value. `dsolve` solves continuous-time models and `rsolve` discrete-time ones.

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
@syms t::nonneg n::positive r::positive K::positive R::positive n₀::positive m::positive
```

## Exponential growth

```{julia}
dsolve(r * n, n, t; ic = n₀), rsolve(R * n, n, t)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert dsolve(r * n, n, t; ic = n₀) == n₀ * exp(r * t)
@assert rsolve(R * n, n, t) == n₀ * R^t
```

## Logistic growth

The logistic equation is separable, and also a Bernoulli equation. The
solution rises from `n₀` towards `K`.

```{julia}
nt = dsolve(r * n * (1 - n / K), n, t; ic = n₀)
```

```{julia}
limit(nt, t, ∞)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(diff(nt, t), r * nt * (1 - nt / K))
@assert isequiv(subs(nt, t => 0), n₀)
@assert limit(nt, t, ∞) == K
```

How long until the population reaches half its carrying capacity?

```{julia}
t_half = only(solve(nt ~ K / 2, t))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(subs(nt, t => t_half), K / 2)
```

## Immigration into a declining or growing population

`n(t+1) = R n(t) + m` is linear. Its solution approaches the equilibrium
`m/(1 - R)` when `R < 1`.

```{julia}
imm = rsolve(R * n + m, n, t)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
f(x) = R * x + m
@assert isequiv(subs(imm, t => 3), f(f(f(n₀))))
```

## Beverton–Holt

A linear-fractional map becomes linear in `1/n`, and `rsolve` uses that
transformation.

```{julia}
bh = rsolve(R * n / (1 + (R - 1) * n / K), n, t)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
g(x) = R * x / (1 + (R - 1) * x / K)
@assert isequiv(subs(bh, t => 2), g(g(n₀)))
```

## Haploid selection

In discrete time the allele frequency is the initial frequency weighted by the
fitnesses raised to the number of generations:

```{julia}
@syms p::(0, 1) p₀::(0, 1) WA::positive Wa::positive s::positive
pt = rsolve(p * WA / (p * WA + (1 - p) * Wa), p, t; ic = p₀)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
h(x) = x * WA / (x * WA + (1 - x) * Wa)
@assert isequiv(subs(pt, t => 2), h(h(p₀)))
@assert isequiv(pt, p₀ * WA^t / (p₀ * WA^t + (1 - p₀) * Wa^t))
```

In continuous time `dp/dt = s p (1 - p)` gives a logistic curve in the allele
frequency. The time for a beneficial allele to go from `p₀` to frequency `p₁`
follows by solving for `t`.

```{julia}
pc = dsolve(s * p * (1 - p), p, t; ic = p₀)
```

```{julia}
@syms p₁::(0, 1)
t₁ = only(solve(pc ~ p₁, t))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(diff(pc, t), s * pc * (1 - pc))
@assert isequiv(subs(pc, t => t₁), p₁)
```
